newsitem.title: FINLAND: BIGGER INCOME TAX CUT IF 98 PAY RISES LOW - NIINISTO.
newsitem.headline: BIGGER INCOME TAX CUT IF 98 PAY RISES LOW - NIINISTO.

text.p: Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said on Wednesday that 1998 income tax cuts could be bigger if the incomes settlement talks lead to modest pay rises from February 1998 onwards.
"A moderate pay deal is something for which even I could be ready to take a slight tax risk, that is to have some confidence in (tax) dynamics," Niinisto told reporters.
He has earlier repeatedly scorned those who claim the state would get back all it loses in income tax cuts thanks to the dynamic effects of increased consumption.
In a speech earlier on Wednesday, Niinisto said the government would stick with its policy of further income tax cuts until the end of the election period in 1999.
He said income tax cuts introduced in 1996 and 1997 would be worth a total of eight billion markka, he said in the speech.
Incomes settlement talks for pay deals due to start in February 1998 are scheduled for the autumn of 1997.
